events.label: Public First POLITICO Poll on deportations August 2026

slots.name: non-MAGA too aggressive
slots.sentence: Non-MAGA Trump voters are twice as likely as self-identified MAGA voters to say the president’s mass deportation campaign is too aggressive — 31 percent compared with 15 percent, according to the new poll, which was conducted Aug. 8 to Aug. 12.

slots.name: observed deportation shift
slots.sentence: A 56 percent majority of Americans say there has been at least a small shift in the way the Trump administration has been conducting its deportation campaign.

slots.name: no trust difference
slots.sentence: But a plurality of those respondents, 44 percent, say the shifts have made no difference in how much they trust the administration on immigration.

slots.name: Trump voter no difference
slots.sentence: Among the 71 percent of Trump voters who said they’ve observed at least a small shift from the administration, nearly half, 48 percent, say those shifts make “no difference” in how much they trust the administration on immigration. Nineteen percent said the shifts make them less likely to trust the administration, while 29 percent said they’d be more likely.

slots.name: MAGA support implementation
slots.sentence: Nearly two-thirds of MAGA Trump voters — 64 percent — say they support both the goals and implementation of his deportations campaign, compared to just 35 percent of non-MAGA Trump voters.

slots.name: poll sample size
slots.sentence: This edition of The POLITICO Poll was conducted by Public First from August 8 to 12, surveying 2,004 U.S. adults online. The overall margin of error is ±2.2 percentage points.

slots.name: more trust likelihood
slots.sentence: while 29 percent said they’d be more likely.
